rows.citation: Gray, R., Kelly, D. (2010). Investigating test selection techniques for scientific software using Hook's mutation sensitivity testing. Procedia Computer Science, 1(1), 1487-1494.
rows.model_type: general scientific software (mutated numerical functions); not neuron models
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - reanalyses Hook's mutation sensitivity experiments in which eight functions were mutated and run against 1155 test cases.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - many test inputs per function (hand-picked versus randomly selected), not physiological stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - generic numerical function outputs; no voltage traces or electrophysiological features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - compares test-selection strategies by mutant detection (random inputs beat hand-picked for four of eight functions); no explicit set-cover selection in abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - abstract mentions extending random-test analysis to additional functions; no frozen discovery/held-out split described (full text blocked).
rows.ai_transformations: no - mutants are seeded code faults; no AI-assisted edits.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Generic precedent for mutation-driven test selection and a random-input baseline in scientific code. NeuroSem moves this to NeuroML neuron models: current-clamp protocols, eFEL features with refinement-calibrated tolerances, admissible-mutant classification, cost-matched random batteries, held-out models and mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1016/j.procs.2010.04.165 (title, authors, vol 1 issue 1 pp 1487-1494, May 2010); abstract from OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar APIs (DBLP id journals/procedia/GrayK10). ScienceDirect PDF blocked (HTTP 403), full text not read.
rows.found_via: Crossref: 'mutation testing scientific simulation software'; metadata confirmed via Crossref /works/<doi> [fallback source used because arXiv/OpenAlex were rate-limited]

rows.citation: Lei, C.L., Clerx, M., Gavaghan, D.J., et al. (2022). Model-driven optimal experimental design for calibrating cardiac electrophysiology models. bioRxiv (published 2023 in Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine, 240, 107690).
rows.model_type: cardiac ventricular action-potential ODE models (O'Hara 2011 plus other published AP models); voltage- and current-clamp
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - samples and infers maximum-conductance scalings for sensitivity and identifiability; no recorded single-fault model edits or regression mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - derives 12 optimised voltage-clamp and 6 current-clamp protocols and compares them with literature benchmark protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - mainly fits whole traces; also tests biomarker-based inference (e.g. APD, AP amplitude, resting potential) and shows noise-induced biomarker biases.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - optimises protocol design variables using local and global sensitivity based A-, D- and E*-optimal criteria with global optimisation.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - protocols designed on O'Hara or an averaged model are assessed on other AP models; no held-out fault family or frozen split.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted model or code transformations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Optimises continuous protocol designs for parameter identifiability in cardiac models. NeuroSem instead selects a discrete protocol subset to detect behaviour-changing edits in NeuroML neuron models, scored by mutant detection coverage under calibrated tolerances against canonical and cost-matched random baselines.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works for bioRxiv DOI (posted 2022-11-02, relation is-preprint-of 10.1016/j.cmpb.2023.107690) and for the journal DOI (vol 240, article 107690, Oct 2023); Europe PMC (PPR566325; PMID 37478675); methods read from bioRxiv full-text PDF; code repo confirmed via github.com redirect and gh api (created 2021-07-15, BSD-3-Clause).

rows.citation: Mandge, D., Jaquier, A., Damart, T.P.L., et al. (2026). BluePyEModel (version 1.0.47). Zenodo.
rows.model_type: detailed (morphological) NEURON e-models fitted to patch-clamp data; NEURON-only, not NeuroML
rows.controlled_mutations: no - parameters vary during optimisation, but no seeded single-fault mutants or valid transformations are described.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - runs sets of optimisation protocols and separate validation protocols derived from patch-clamp recordings on each e-model.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - extracts e-features via eFEL and BluePyEfe and scores models on them.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - optimises model parameters against feature targets; protocols come from data or configuration, not selected for fault detection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - validation step can run protocols not used in optimisation; no held-out models or mutation families for a detection method.
rows.ai_transformations: no - none described in README or Zenodo metadata.
rows.software: BluePyEModel, https://github.com/openbraininstitute/BluePyEModel (Apache-2.0 per README and DataCite; PyPI bluepyemodel 1.0.47)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Builds and validates e-models against experimental features. NeuroSem compares a transformed NeuroML model with its own reference, calibrates tolerances by numerical refinement, measures detection power with controlled mutants, and selects a compact battery. BluePyEModel/BluePyEfe protocol and feature configurations are reusable inputs.
rows.verification_method: DataCite API for 10.5281/zenodo.19593077 (creators, version 1.0.47, issued 2026-09-09, Apache-2.0); CITATION.cff (date-released 2023-08-25) and README via GitHub REST API; GitHub repo metadata (license API reports NOASSERTION); PyPI JSON (1.0.47 uploaded 2026-09-09, requires Python >=3.11; examples CC-BY-NC-SA per license text).

rows.citation: Pierpoint, G.B., Liu, Y. (2026). Numerical Validation for Cell-Matched Neuronal Model Replay (version 0.2.1). Zenodo.
rows.model_type: Allen Cell Types cell-matched neuron models (perisomatic biophysical and GLIF) replayed with recorded stimuli; synthetic current-delivery benchmark
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - compares playback methods, solver steps and equilibration durations as analysis conditions; no single-fault mutant generation or classification.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - five synthetic waveforms plus Allen recording selections (e.g. Long Square) across 72 condition-specific cases.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - spike count, first-spike latency and steady-state voltage errors; no broader eFEL feature battery.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no protocol selection or battery optimisation.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - one method-development cell kept apart from five evaluation cells; README explicitly disclaims held-out prediction claims.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted transformations described in README or methodology document.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Checks numerical fidelity of stimulus delivery and initial-state equilibration in model replay, not detection of behaviour changes after model edits. Its solver-step refinement, material-change thresholds and never-zero non-evaluable outcomes closely parallel NeuroSem tolerance and undefined-feature rules; cite it there. No mutants or protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: DataCite API for 10.5281/zenodo.21483417 (creators, v0.2.1, issued 2026-07-21, MIT); CITATION.cff, README and docs/METHODOLOGY_AND_SCOPE.md via GitHub REST API (solver steps 0.025-0.0025 ms, 0.025 ms / 0.5 mV material-change criteria, reason-coded non-evaluable outcomes); repo created 2026-07-22. Manuscript anonymous; no paper DOI found.
rows.found_via: GitHub search neuron model validation; DOI badge in README; DataCite API; also DataCite Zenodo query neuronal model replay validation

rows.citation: Koch, N.A., Sonnenberg, L., Hedrich, U.B.S., et al. (2023). Loss or gain of function? Effects of ion channel mutations on neuronal firing depend on the neuron type. Frontiers in Neurology, 14, 1194811.
rows.model_type: single-compartment conductance-based neuron models of diverse types (e.g. FS, RS pyramidal, RS inhibitory, Cb stellate, STN); Python, forward Euler
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - one-factor-at-a-time changes to properties of shared currents (e.g. gating half-activation shifts of -10 to +10 mV) plus KCNA1 mutation parameter sets.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - 200 two-second current steps forming fI curves plus an ascending/descending ramp; one protocol family, not a diverse battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - rheobase and area under the initial fI curve from steady-state firing; adaptation deliberately excluded; not eFEL.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - fixed step and ramp protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - compares perturbation effects across models; no discovery/held-out split.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Studies how controlled biophysical perturbations change firing across neuron types to interpret channelopathies. NeuroSem instead treats such perturbations as mutants to measure whether regression batteries detect them, with calibrated tolerances, protocol selection and held-out models. Its neuron-type dependence supports multi-model evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works for journal DOI (vol 14, article 1194811, 2023-05-24, CC BY 4.0) and bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2023.01.16.524256; Europe PMC core record (PMID 37292138, PMC10244640) and fullTextXML methods sections 2.2-2.3; GitHub REST API repo metadata (MIT) and README.

rows.citation: Hough, M. (2026). hnn-jax: differentiable JAX reimplementation of the HNN forward model [software]. GitHub.
rows.model_type: neocortical column network model (HNN / hnn_core on NEURON) producing current-dipole output, reimplemented in JAX/Diffrax
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no fault seeding; regressions guarded by a ratcheted forward-correlation threshold against the reference.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Sobol-sampled drive parameters plus zero-drive and graded-drive metamorphic tests; exogenous synaptic drives, not current-clamp protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares dipole waveform correlation and amplitude, not single-cell electrophysiological features.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - oracle comparison over parameter samples; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: unclear - README does not say whether the translation was AI-assisted; linked nsg-agent-kit not examined.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Differential and metamorphic testing of one simulator translation at network-dipole level. NeuroSem targets single-neuron NeuroML edits, calibrates per-feature tolerances by refinement, quantifies detection with controlled mutants and selects protocols. Its report that hnn_core versions give different references supports strict simulator-version pinning.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo metadata (created 2026-07-27, MIT), README and tests/test_oracle_contract.py via GitHub API, LICENSE (copyright Morgan Hough), GitHub users API for m9h display name. No DOI or paper found.
